digest.component_or_area: verifier model-class resolution across LLM config, plan-review, completion, and code-review gates
propositions: Three separate verifier-selection paths break off the default provider, so any non-default (e.g. Bedrock) model reads as an operator override and the verifier downgrade silently stops applying.
code-review.yaml declares no model on its steps, so all four code-review passes never downgrade and Pass-2's temperature:0 greedy verification loses determinism on the frontier model.

The fix introduces one shared resolve_model_string that treats trivial/standard/frontier as reserved values, returns any literal model id unchanged, and is called from each verifier call site instead of comparing cfg.model to a constant.
Pass-2/Pass-4 verifier paths must resolve the standard class regardless of cfg.model, including provider-qualified ids like anthropic:claude-opus-4-8 that the old exact-match heuristic missed.

A regression exists where resolve_class always emits a provider-qualified id, so with no class configured the verifier model string changes form (bare vs qualified), breaking the promised byte-identical back-compat.
_verifier_cfg must be verified through its real callers (xcheck contradiction and comment-trail entries) so a caller passing plain cfg would leave passes on the frontier model and be caught.
